column3: NASB follows the critical text (“heaven”); “give” is rendered “grant.”
NASB renders “continue steadfastly in prayer” as “Devote yourselves to prayer” and “watching” as “keeping alert,” and adds “an attitude of.”
NASB renders “declare” as “speak forth” and “have been bound” as “have … been imprisoned.”
NASB renders “as it behooves me” as “in the way I ought.”
NASB renders “walk” as “Conduct yourselves” and “redeeming the time” as “making the most of the opportunity.”
NASB adds “as it were” and renders “answer” as “respond.”
NASB renders “all the things concerning me” as “all my affairs” and “will make known” as “will bring you information.”
NASB follows the critical text (“that you may know about our circumstances”).
NASB adds “with him” and “our,” and renders “of you” as “one of your number.”
NASB adds “sends you his greetings” and puts the instruction about Mark in parentheses. A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
NASB restructures the verse; “comfort” is rendered “encouragement.”
NASB reads “Jesus Christ,” the order of other manuscripts; it follows the critical text (“fully assured”) and renders “servant” as “bondslave.”
NASB follows the critical text (“deep concern”).
NASB follows the critical text (“Nympha … her house”).
NASB adds “this” and renders “the one from Laodicea” as “my letter that is coming from Laodicea.”
NASB follows the critical text without “Amen” and the Textus Receptus subscription; it restructures the greeting and renders “chains” as “imprisonment.”
